prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve / illustration-story. One finished standalone Kalistar painted illustration, NOT a card. REQUIRED OUTPUT COMPOSITION: portrait aspect 737:921 (approximately 4:5), wider than reference image 1. Edge-to-edge painted world, no text, borders, interface, logos or statistics.
References: image 1 is the first TRAINING painting to revise; preserve this exact young woman's identity, clothes, rainbow tattoo designs and painterly world, but RECOMPOSE the fencing action and camera distance. Image 2 is the canonical Kaylis identity source and must remain recognizably the same 23-year-old Indian/Afro-Caribbean mixed woman with warm medium-brown skin and dark eyes. Images 3 Momo and 4 Valazar are style only: painterly colour planes, selective oil/gouache strokes, worn materials, nuanced expression. Do not copy their characters. Not anime, manga, CGI, photographic skin, airbrushed model or artificially grained image.

Primary correction: the COMPLETE head including tied braids AND the entire long rapier from pommel to pointed tip must be within the image with generous safety margin. Pull the camera back and reshape the gesture, NOT shorten the weapon. Reserve at least 10 percent canvas height of visible sky ABOVE the topmost hair, and at least 10 percent canvas height of stone ground BELOW both complete boots. The figure is approximately 78 percent of the picture height, with face still expressive. The FULL blade, guard, hilt and weapon hand lie in the central 75 percent of the width, never leaving the picture.

Draw one elegant single long fencing foil/rapier with a slender, perfectly straight continuous steel blade about arm-length, believable adult proportions, a coherent modest cup/swept guard and a hand firmly wrapped around its hilt. Stage the guard near the centre of her torso at about 55 percent image height, the blade running diagonally upward toward the viewer's upper right, tip around 73 percent width and 18 percent height. It may aim slightly toward the viewer, with modest coherent perspective, but must remain visibly a LONG straight blade, not a short dagger or a wide fantasy sword. The blade and hand/grip/guard share one credible unbroken axis. The blade MUST NOT run horizontally out of the image. Clean silhouette against sky and quiet stone. No multiple blades, bent sword, disconnected tip, ghost blade or compressed shortened rapier.

Kaylis is mid-turn in fencing training, beautiful purposeful action rather than posing. Front boot planted and knee bent, rear foot following the pivot, shoulders counter-rotated; sword elbow bent so the hilt stays near the centre; free hand balances compactly and stays in the central area. Focused confident half-smile, her gaze following the imagined opponent and her blade. This is agile practiced training with a sense of spin in the braids and trouser folds, not a static wide-legged fashion pose. Same slightly muscular physique, same face and existing curling vine-like prismatic arm tattoos. Hair black, braided and tied back with a few identity-defining loose curls. EXACT outfit: fitted BLACK SLEEVELESS TURTLENECK, WHITE full-length practical trousers, BLACK training boots. Both muscular arms bare, rainbow light restrained and visible on both arms.

Keep the first painting's constructed red-grey stone practice platforms raised by Balmhyr, quiet distant Canyonero cliffs and broad clear blue sky, natural warm daylight and cool painted shadows. Balmhyr is absent. Architecture and clouds are broad restrained shapes, visually calmer than the character. No other people or additional objects. One head, two arms with coherent hands, two legs; no duplicated limbs or motion echoes. Paint the face as naturally as the original Kalistar references. All changes are generated coherently as one painting, not patchwork.
